concept.title: API conventions
concept.shortdesc: Use these conventions when reading BPM OpenAPI contracts and building integration requests.

section.title: Base URLs and discovery
section.p: Examples use $BPM_BASE_URL as a deployment value. Discover the current contract from /openapi.json and, for interactive inspection only, the FastAPI schema UIs at /docs and /redoc. Product documentation is available at /help/; do not use /docs as its route.

section.title: Content types
section.p: Most programmatic operations use JSON request and response bodies. Firefox import accepts application/json and multipart/form-data; unsupported media types can return 415. Firefox export returns application/json and can add Content-Disposition when download output is requested.

section.title: Identifiers and lifecycle
section.p: Profile IDs are integer path identifiers owned by BPM. Store the returned id and revision after create, import, read, and update operations. Profile names are unique and cannot be changed through ProfileUpdate. Lifecycle values are active, archived, and all; include_deleted is a compatibility flag that must be interpreted together with lifecycle.

section.title: Models and schema channels
section.p: ProfileCreate, ProfileUpdate, and ProfileRead are BPM normalized profile shapes. The Firefox boundary document is exactly a top-level object with one policies object: {"policies":{...}}. On JSON import that boundary is the document member of the BPM request; export returns that boundary alone. Profile ID, schema version, revision, compliance, and other BPM metadata are never members of policies.json. Validation uses ValidationRequest and supported schema channels such as Firefox ESR and Release; a plain policy mapping remains compatibility behavior, not the preferred external shape.

POST /api/profiles/prepare/new accepts only NewProfilePreparationRequest: name, target_schema_id, starter_id, cis_baseline_id, and an opaque preparation_idempotency_key. POST /api/profiles/prepare/duplicate adds source_id and expected_source_revision. Callers cannot submit flags, compliance, provenance, or a conversion candidate. The server derives one saved ProfileRead; an exact accepted-key replay returns that result. The read-only POST /api/profiles/prepare/duplicate/preview accepts source and catalog identities without an idempotency key and returns a value-free DuplicateProfilePreparationPreview.

section.title: Filtering, sorting, and pagination
section.p: Profile list and stats operations support search, schema, validation state, lifecycle, and include-deleted filters. List pagination is offset/limit with default limit=50, maximum 200, and offset=0. Sorting uses current described fields such as created_at, updated_at, name, schema_version, and id, with asc or desc order.

section.title: Status and error handling
section.p: Use status codes and body shape together. 200, 201, and 204 are success families, but validation can return 200 with ok=false. Error bodies use FastAPI detail and may contain a string, a validation list, or a BPM object with message, error, or issues. Preparation errors are the explicit stable ProfilePreparationErrorEnvelope; every terminal preparation error carries detail.kind="profile-preparation-error", contract_version=1, locale-neutral code, i18n_key, http_status, mutation="none", and value-free parameters. A blocked duplicate conversion, stale source, unavailable catalog choice, name conflict, or failed transaction creates no target and does not change the source. Conversion preview and apply use their own value-free detail envelope with locale-neutral code, mutation=none on every error, and retry_preview_required when a fresh preview is needed.

section.title: Public profile preparation
section.p: POST /api/profiles/prepare/new accepts only a name and the target_schema_id, starter_id, cis_baseline_id, and preparation_idempotency_key identities. POST /api/profiles/prepare/duplicate also accepts source_id and expected_source_revision; POST /api/profiles/prepare/duplicate/preview is read-only. Callers cannot submit flags, compliance, provenance, or a conversion candidate. A terminal ProfilePreparationErrorEnvelope with mutation="none" creates no target and does not change the source.
